With election day three days away, early voting has just wrapped up in Georgia, where Democrats

Political campaigns are making their push for final votes, and increasingly, that means
sending text messages directly to your cell phone.
Texas Public Radio's David Martin Davies has more.

This week, one of the biggest heists in the history of cryptocurrency took place, as hackers

And here's Stephen Vassaja has more.
These stock drops look even steeper when you zoom out to the past month.
Facebook's parent company, Meta, is down more than 15 percent.
Google's parent company, Alphabet, down more than 18 percent.
Intel down more than 45 percent.
This sell-off sped up as tech companies updated investors about the massive amounts of money
they are spending on AI, particularly on data centers.
That's given investors sticker shock.
Other parts of the market are also feeling the sting of high oil prices.
Crude oil futures are up, selling at more than $104 a barrel.
Stephen Vassaja, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
King Charles and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham will be in Antigua on Monday for a
summit of leaders of the British Commonwealth.
With Britain's historic role in Caribbean slave plantations, that's emerging as a major
theme.
Vicky Barker has more from London.
King Charles began his first Caribbean tour as king this past week, acknowledging, quote,
"the great suffering caused by slavery."
And in Saturday's Guardian, Prime Minister Andy Burnham expressed similar sentiments.
British lawmaker Bell Ribeiro Addy, though, told the BBC that isn't enough.
"Acknowledgement isn't the same as understanding, and we have still fallen short of a formal
state apology."
Burnham's op-ed suggests that formal apology could come after extensive dialogue.
But he, like his predecessors, has ruled out financial reparations.
For NPR News, I'm Vicky Barker in London.
Some 200 cruise ship passengers on an around-the-world voyage that promoted its cabins as floating
homes are now scrambling for other accommodations.
This after the MV Odyssey said it can't afford the gas to sail the ship.
That ship set sail two years ago on a voyage to seven continents, offering an ad to make
the Odyssey a permanent floating home.
But without warning this week, passengers, who are mostly Americans, were given hours

The fate of the ship isn't certain, and some passengers say they sold their homes to buy

topics.text: Early voting wraps in Georgia as Democrats seek to re-elect Senator Jon Ossoff and win governor's race
